label: F-8b2bc7

findings.note: The plan decides this: §8 (plan line 655-656) says a torn file 'reads as no cooldown with one warning (S19) and is overwritten whole by the next park', and the doc comment at QuotaCooldowns.cs:184-186 says the same; the 'refuse on unreadable re-read' requirement is not in the plan, which only refuses I/O failures.

This is the same point as index 0: QuotaCooldowns.cs:194 treats a non-version-1 or null-entries file as unreadable and the next write replaces it whole, which the plan decided on purpose (fail open, D4 and §8).

The plan's §11 (line 809) rejected an entry cap because eviction could un-park a spent row; ResetOfAsync at QuotaCooldowns.cs:371 already turns a past reset into a future guess, and stated waits are capped by MaxStatedWait.
Plan D6 says outright that the probe reuses the refused launch's request with 'the same environment (ANTIGRAVITY_API_KEY when set)', because /quota needs the same sign-in.

PlanAsync (QuotaCooldowns.cs:318-334) follows D5: a spent refusal wins over Ok, an undecided agy refusal whose gauge reads Available is transient, and the plan says a key with an Ok and no qualifying refusal is lifted; the text is muddled and names no wrong outcome.

Plan D6 says a past reset_time is SpentWithoutReset ('a past instant is no reset, never a park on the past') and goes the stated/guess road, so the guard at QuotaCooldowns.cs:371 does what the plan asks; an Available gauge never carries a past instant (AntigravityRuntime.cs:212 builds it with StatedOrGuess).

CoolingReasonOf (PanelService.cs:451-454) answers only when AuthFor(provider).Auth != "unavailable", so a missing credential still gets its auth reason, and RowRefusal is checked before cooling in ReasonFor.

There is no deadlock (the lock is a separate file, QuotaCooldowns.cs:76), and Apply (:387-394) keeps the live order of the kept entries, so SequenceEqual is false only on a real change (a park always changes SinceUtc); the escaping IOException is the documented refusal path (:185-186), and 'Blocking' is unfounded.

Consecutive is computed twice, once in ResetOfAsync (QuotaCooldowns.cs:366) and again inside the lock in EntryOf (:400, on purpose so processes agree), so an entry that expires during the up-to-30 s probe can store 0 against a longer backoff; the only effect is a counter restart, which the plan wants after expiry anyway.

It cannot crash: the entry came from Standing a moment earlier, so 'left' can be negative by at most microseconds, and (long)Math.Ceiling(-0.0001) is 0, giving 'in 0 min' rather than an overflow or '-0 min' (PanelService.cs:440-447).

AgyError.cs:26 rejoins the whole rest of stderr for every AGY_ERROR marker, which is quadratic in the number of markers; in practice stderr holds one or two markers, so the impact is small, and calling it Security is overstated.

ClaudeRuntime.RateLimited (:179) parses the envelope exactly as the measured WhyItFailed already does (:155); the CLI's JSON envelope is the whole of stdout, and the plan's D7 specifies this envelope read.

PlanAllAsync (QuotaCooldowns.cs:283-289) probes one key at a time with a 30 s timeout each, so up to three refused agy keys can add about 90 s after the round; this happens only on refused agy rows, and the plan specifies no progress notice.
Plan D4 says 'read on every CanRun, no cache (it is under 16 KiB for ever)', and Standing at QuotaCooldowns.cs:96-97 does exactly that by design.

Classified (ReviewerExecutor.cs:1016) calls the adapter's RateLimited on every launch, and ClaudeRuntime.cs:179 parses all of stdout before checking ExitCode != 0 at :180, so every successful review is parsed for nothing; checking the exit code first is a trivial fix.

summary: Of 15 findings, only two small efficiency points (AgyError's repeated rejoin and Claude's parse before the exit-code check) are real, and two more are partly real, low-impact edge points. Most of the rest ask for things the plan explicitly decided against (overwriting a torn file, no entry cap, reusing the agy environment, no read cache) or misread the code, including a garbled 'Blocking' deadlock claim.
